action: Fugaku users: revoke and replace SSH keys used with Fugaku, as RIKEN asks, and watch for phishing emails. Others: no action needed; for awareness.
date_note: Intrusion ran November 10-13 and Fugaku was shut down November 14; date is RIKEN's public notice of November 16.
exec: A national research supercomputer is offline with no restart date, and stolen credentials were used to connect to external systems.
impact: Fugaku has been shut down since November 14 and users' login keys were disabled.
plain: Japan's Fugaku supercomputer is still offline. RIKEN says 4,222 Fugaku users were affected and 430 login credentials were exfiltrated; some were used to connect to other systems.

evidence.quote: from November 10 to 13, 2026, an external third party gained unauthorized access to Fugaku's internal operational network by using a publicly accessible web page displaying Fugaku's operational status (the dashboard).
430 credentials, including private keys, were collected and exfiltrated from some users' home directories.

summary: RIKEN's first notice says an outside party reached Fugaku's internal operational network from November 10 to 13 through a public web page showing Fugaku's operational status; the exact method is under investigation. Its second notice (20 Nov) lists 4,222 Fugaku users as affected and says 430 credentials (233 SSH private keys without a passphrase, 197 with one) were exfiltrated; some were used for external connections. Fugaku stays offline; no attacker is named.
title: Japan's RIKEN takes Fugaku supercomputer offline after intrusion

validation.note: Primary: RIKEN's first notice (dated Nov. 17 on the page; the second notice calls it the notice of November 16) and second notice of 20 Nov, both read. The first notice gives the November 10-13 intrusion via the public operational-status dashboard, detection of suspicious traffic on November 12, confirmation on November 13 and suspension at 4:30 AM on November 14. The Register, ITdaily, eSecurity Planet and Hacked.com relay RIKEN's statements. The second notice gives 4,222 Fugaku users; the first notice's section 3 says up to 4,224.

review.note: Stronger than the source: summary/plain said 4,222 users' data was taken; RIKEN lists 4,222 as affected and says 430 credentials were exfiltrated. Dates, 233/197 keys, offline status match
